newsitem.title: USA: IBM, Intel in pact to cut costs of Networked PCs.
newsitem.headline: IBM, Intel in pact to cut costs of Networked PCs.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp and Intel Corp on Wednesday said they have entered into an agreement that will reduce the support costs of high-performance Networked Personal Computers.

In their Advanced Manageability Alliance, the two firms said they will use thier combined expertise to reduce customer network downtime; simplify desktop administration, client installation and upgrades; and lower total costs of ownership.
In the first stage of the alliance, Intel, through its network unit, will incorporate Wake On LAN remote management capability into its Fast Ethernet LAN adapters and LANDesk Client Manager software.

IBM's subsidiary, IBM PC Co, will incorporate those Intel products into its commercial desktop computers featuring Pentium Pro and Pentium processors, which will be available in the first quarter of 1997.
The firms said they will also offer IBM's LAN Client Control Manager and Intel's LANDesk Configuration Manager, software that will simplify the support of corporate PCs.

This new work will complement the companies' joint efforts to integrate enterprise systems and desktop management capabilities, involving the Tivoli Systems TME 10 NetFinity product and Intel's LANDesk management products, the firms said.

"(The alliance) recognizes that organizations require adaptable, connected PCs to run their business successfully and also need to control support costs," said Frank Gill, executive vice president, Intel. "This work furthers our effort to reduce the total cost of ownership without sacrificing necessary flexibility and performance."
